strings.name: Mohammad Javad Zarif
strings.role: Former Iranian foreign minister; founder and president of PAIAB
strings.summary: Mohammad Javad Zarif is an Iranian diplomat and scholar who served as ambassador to the United Nations and foreign minister from 2013 to 2021, leading Iran’s team in the 2015 nuclear negotiations. His career spans multilateral bargaining, US sanctions and domestic policy disputes. After leaving the strategic affairs vice presidency in 2025, he continued advocating regional dialogue through teaching, research and public debate.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 18 November 2026, with recent activity supported by the 23 September Islamabad roundtable report and an article dated 8 November. Current and former posts, resignation and its acceptance, and proposals and enacted state arrangements are distinguished. Old footage recirculated in 2026 is not treated as a new speech that year.
strings.influence.rationale: His service as Iran’s foreign minister and participation in nuclear negotiations shape understanding of Iran’s international relations and regional policies.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and education
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in Tehran on 8 January 1960. He earned a BA and MA in international relations at San Francisco State University in 1981 and 1982, followed by an MA and PhD in international studies at the University of Denver in 1984 and 1988. Degree names follow the awarding university’s account and are distinguished from his dissertation’s international-law subject.
strings.facts.f2.label: Diplomatic and academic background
strings.facts.f2.value: He worked at Iran’s UN mission in the 1980s and later combined diplomatic practice with university teaching. PAIAB’s current CV lists him as its founder and president and an associate professor of global studies at the University of Tehran. His initiatives do not automatically constitute Iranian government decisions.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Negotiating achievements and subsequent limits
strings.highlights.h1.text: He shared the 2016 Chatham House Prize with John Kerry for their roles in the nuclear negotiations. The agreement resulted from multiple parties and teams. The US withdrew in 2018 and implementation later suffered repeated setbacks; agreement on a text in 2015 did not permanently resolve the dispute.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Continuing advocacy of regional dialogue
strings.highlights.h2.text: He discussed shared security in Islamabad in September 2026 and co-authored an 8 November essay with Ali Nasri advocating dialogue and ethical constraints on power drawn from different civilizations. These are publicly advanced ideas and policy proposals, not a newly concluded treaty or proof that peace has been achieved.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Vice-presidential resignation formally accepted
strings.timeline.t1.text: After he tendered his resignation in March, Pezeshkian formally accepted it late on 15 April and appointed Mohsen Ismaili as vice president for strategic affairs. Early-March reporting said the president had not yet responded; submission and acceptance should not be dated as the same event.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Appointed vice president for strategic affairs
strings.timeline.t2.text: Pezeshkian appointed him to work on the new government’s strategic affairs. He offered to resign in August but returned later that month. This episode differs from his final departure approved in 2025 and did not make him first vice president or foreign minister again.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Foreign-ministerial term ends
strings.timeline.t3.text: As Raisi formed his government, parliament approved Hossein Amirabdollahian as foreign minister, ending Zarif’s eight years in Rouhani’s administration. His later strategic affairs vice presidency was a separate office.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Placed under US sanctions
strings.timeline.t4.text: The US Treasury imposed sanctions under Executive Order 13876, stating that he acted for or on behalf of Iran’s supreme leader. This records a US administrative designation and its stated grounds, not a conviction by the International Criminal Court.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Nuclear agreement text concluded
strings.timeline.t5.text: In Vienna, he completed negotiations on the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action with EU and six-country representatives and announced the outcome jointly with Mogherini. The agreed text, Implementation Day on 16 January 2016 and subsequent compliance are distinct stages. The deal was not devised by just two US and Iranian individuals.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Parliament approves him as foreign minister
strings.timeline.t6.text: Rouhani’s nominee received 232 votes in favour and took charge of the foreign ministry, subsequently leading Iran’s nuclear negotiating team. The minister negotiates and implements policy but is not Iran’s sole foreign-policy decision-maker.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becomes permanent representative to the UN
strings.timeline.t7.text: He began serving as Iran’s permanent representative in New York, remaining until 2007 and engaging in multilateral diplomacy. He represented Iran, not the UN secretary-general; holding positions in UN bodies did not make him head of the organization.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Becomes deputy foreign minister for legal and international affairs
strings.timeline.t8.text: He entered the ministry’s senior leadership, overseeing legal and international affairs until 2002. This deputy-ministerial service preceded his UN ambassadorship and foreign-ministerial term and should not be combined into one continuous tenure as foreign minister.
